text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High p95 latency for inference.redwood.api in eu-west-1 — sustained > 850ms for 5m, error rate +1.8%. Trigger: latency-slo-2min. Paging noah (oncall).
noah (oncall): on it. paging tess and ajay. starting timeline notes.
noah (oncall): quick-check: is this across all models or only some?
ajay (runtime): looks worse for long-context generation tasks (seq >= 1024). short requests p95 fine. logs show increased tail across g4dn clusters.
tess (sre): seeing elevated queue depth on serving pool eu-west-gpu-pool-3, autoscaler hasn't added capacity in last 4m.
maria (prodops): we have a scheduled maintenance window ending in 20m for the eu-west control-plane — could be correlated. tagging infra.
noah (oncall): ok, triage plan: (1) open mitigation window, (2) enable fallback routing to eu-central for non-data-resident tenants, (3) temporarily increase pool target for eu-west-gpu-pool-3, (4) draft statuspage + customer notice.
ajay (runtime): can enable model-variant fallback for higher-latency-tolerant routes. propose: route heavy-gen -> smaller quantized model (m-1q) for 15m while we scale. command:
```
# increase pool replicas
rwctl pool scale --env eu-west --pool eu-west-gpu-pool-3 --replicas 12
# enable fallback policy
rwctl route update --route inference.redwood.api --fallback-model m-1q --scope long-seq
```
noah (oncall): +1 to both. do we anticipate quality regressions? need to warn customers.
ajay (runtime): yes minor decrease for long-tail tokens but usually OK for brevity use cases. we'll mark as best-effort fallback.
ryan (support): I'll prep a short customer-facing snippet we can paste into status page and customer emails. Drafting now.
statuspage-bot: DRAFT: "We are investigating elevated inference latency in eu-west-1 affecting long-generation requests. Engineers are applying mitigations including routing to alternative regions and temporary model fallbacks. No data loss. Some requests may see reduced response fidelity. Estimated restoration: 30–60 minutes."
noah (oncall): tweak: say "expected partial restoration in 15–30 minutes after scaling completes". keep conservative for full restoration.
statuspage-bot: UPDATED DRAFT: "We are investigating elevated inference latency in eu-west-1 affecting long-generation requests. Engineers are applying mitigations including routing to alternative regions and temporary model fallbacks. No data loss. Expected partial restoration in 15–30 minutes; full recovery may take longer while we stabilize queues."
maria (prodops): tagging legal & compliance for any region routing impact — @tess any PII concerns with routing cross-region?
tess (sre): cross-region routing allowed for most customers; enterprise tenants with restrict-region flag will not be routed. make sure the status note mentions "non-data-resident tenants only" where applicable.
ryan (support): customer email draft: "Hi — we’re responding to increased response times in our EU region which may affect long-generation requests. We have activated fallbacks (smaller model / alternative region) to reduce latency; you may notice small changes in output. No data was exposed. We’ll send updates as we have them. — Redwood Inference Ops". Want to include ETA?
noah (oncall): include ETA: "partial restoration expected in 15–30 minutes".
ajay (runtime): mitigation steps in parallel: (A) scale pool -> target 12 replicas, (B) force an immediate rolling restart of one hot-serving subgroup to flush possible KV cache fragmentation:
```
rwctl pool restart-subgroup --pool eu-west-gpu-pool-3 --subgroup hot-1 --rolling
```
noah (oncall): note: rolling restart could spike latency briefly; we should only do it after fallbacks are active.
ajay (runtime): agreed. scheduling restart for +5m after fallback enabled.
noah (oncall): action assignments: ajay -> execute scaling + fallback; tess -> watch autoscaler & infra interactions; maria -> post initial status page + customer notice; ryan -> triage incoming support tickets and use template; noah -> coordinate external comms and runbook. oncall-next -> standby for handoff at 30m.
oncall-next: acknowledged. will be ready to take over at 2173458200.
statuspage-bot: POSTED: Public status page update live (incident id IN-2026-217345).
ryan (support): created internal support-first canned reply for affected customers with placeholders: "[region], [eta], [fallback notes]". Posting here for approval: 
"Hi <customer>,
We’re currently mitigating higher than normal inference latency in EU (eu-west-1) affecting long-generation requests. We’ve enabled temporary fallbacks to a smaller model and routing to nearby regions to reduce latency. Expected partial restoration: 15–30 minutes. No data loss. If you have region-residency requirements, please reply and we’ll ensure your requests stay in-region. — Redwood Support"
noah (oncall): looks good. add line: "If you need immediate consistency/quality guarantees, pause long-generation workloads or pin to a specific model version."
ryan (support): added.
ajay (runtime): scaling command executed at 2173456900, replicas increased to 12. autoscaler metrics show pool CPU/GPU util dropping from 95% -> 68% within 4m.
tess (sre): queue depth trending down, p95 improved from 870ms -> 480ms on short requests, long-gen p95 still ~620ms.
noah (oncall): does telemetry show any error spikes during fallback?
ajay (runtime): failure rate stable; a couple of 503s during initial routing config but <0.2% overall.
maria (prodops): statuspage-bot: POSTED update to enterprise-only feed noting "enterprise restrict-region unaffected".
statuspage-bot: NOTE: sent targeted email to customers with region-restrict flags advising no cross-region routing.
ryan (support): two customers asked for more detail. I've sent them the canned reply and offered to whitelist in-region pinning if needed.
ajay (runtime): starting rolling restart of hot-1 subgroup at 2173457200. will monitor.
tess (sre): be ready to abort if we see latency spike >1s.
ajay (runtime): rolling restart finished at 2173457400. small transient spike but recovered.
noah (oncall): great. summary so far: scaling + fallback + rolling restart applied. visible improvement but not full recovery. ETA update: partial service restored; continue monitoring.
statuspage-bot: UPDATED: "Mitigations applied: scaling, temporary model fallback, and rolling restarts. Partial restoration observed. Engineers continue to monitor. Next update in 15 minutes or sooner if status changes."
maria (prodops): drafting post-incident internal comms template for eng leads: 
"Summary: brief incident description + timeline. Impact: which customers & regions. Mitigation: steps applied with timestamps. Next steps: RCA cadence + postmortem owner. Customer comms: links to public status and sent emails"
noah (oncall): handoff note for oncall-next: "Handoff @2173458200 -> oncall-next: state is mitigations active, partial restoration, watch p95 for long-gen and queue depth. If p95 > 700ms or error rate >1% escalate to SEV-2 and notify eng-sre. All status messages are in status page IN-2026-217345. Use the support canned replies in this thread."
oncall-next: taking over now at 2173458200. thanks team.
noah (oncall): leaving detailed logs + run commands in #incidents-runbooks. tagging postmortem owner suggestion: @maria.
maria (prodops): happy to own postmortem. will schedule RCA with runtime & SRE tomorrow.
statuspage-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed after 2h if stable; otherwise escalate.
noah (oncall): closing notes: add lessons for Optimize team: consider knob to lower KV cache TTL gracefully rather than rolling restart. tag in postmortem.
ryan (support): will send final customer follow-up once we mark resolved. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: RESOLVE: Incident IN-2026-217345 marked as mitigated at 2173458300.
